# Thomas Kabalin

> Third-year Bachelor of Business Science (Computer Science) student at UCT, Vice-Chancellor's Scholar, and Junior Software Engineer at a Cape Town fintech. Interested in software engineering, AI engineering, data science, and the practical application of technology to business problems.

Thomas Kabalin is a South African student and software engineer based in Cape Town, South Africa. As of 2026, he is in his third year of a Bachelor of Business Science (Computer Science) degree at the University of Cape Town (UCT), a four-year programme, with an expected graduation year of 2027. His academic record includes a first-year GPA of 88.13 and a second-year GPA of 85.68.

His professional interests span software engineering, AI engineering, data science, the practical applications of AI, quantitative development, and technology-driven problem solving. He is actively exploring a range of career paths at the intersection of technology and business.

Awards and honours:

## Work Experience

**Junior Software Engineer**
Fynbos Technologies (Fynbos Money) · January 2026–Present
Working part-time as a Junior Backend Engineer contributing to a product that is changing how South Africans invest and grow their wealth. Building hands-on experience in PHP and Laravel, delivering production-ready features through AI-driven engineering workflows. Fynbos is a Cape Town-based fintech focused on making financial products — including tax-free savings accounts and investment accounts — more accessible to South Africans.

## Leadership & Extra-Curricular

**Scientific Committee Member, South African Programming Olympiad (2024–Present)**
Contributes to the design, review, and moderation of national Olympiad tasks for high school learners across South Africa. Responsibilities include setting and refining programming problems and model solutions, reviewing and moderating competition papers, participating in regular committee meetings on contest operations and improvements, and providing on-site support at training camps — including for the 2026 International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI), hosted in Uzbekistan.

**External Moderator, South African Applications Olympiad & Talent Search (2026–Present)**
Serves as one of the primary external moderators of the national Applications Olympiad — a computer literacy contest for high school learners — and the Talent Search, a computational thinking challenge.
